L128: 2. Look at the fabric. Check whether the fabric is straight. L129: L130: • Check that the ends of the fabric are square. Line up the ends of the folded fabric with the corner of a counter or table. Both ends should be even and straight with the corner. L131: L132: Square L133: Not square L134: L135: • If the fabric’s cut edges are not straight, you may need to purchase extra fabric. L136: L137: Lesson 3 — CUTTING EDGE L138: L139: BACKGROUND BASICS...Cutting Edge L140: Fibers are where our fabrics and apparel begin. The generic name is the key word you need to know and understand about textile products. There are two basic types of fibers -- natural (from plants and animals) and manufactured (from chemicals). L141: Natural fibers -- cotton, linen, silk and wool are usually water-loving (very absorbent, and are not heat sensitive). They tend to soil easily but are easily cleaned. Most manufactured fabrics (you may know them best as man-made or synthetic) are usually strong, heat sensitive, and susceptible to static electricity. They do not readily absorb moisture, so they are quick drying. L142: Any of the fibers, natural or manufactured may be made into a variety of fabrics. Today, there is not one best fiber. Each fiber makes a contribution to the world of textiles. Each has its own use. L143: A fiber is the basic unit of textile raw material such as cotton, wool, etc. A yarn is lots fibers twisted together to form a continuous strand which can be used in making fabric. A fabric is any woven, knitted, plaited, braided, felted, or non-woven material made of yarns. Yarns may be a single strand, or two or more yarns twisted together. They may be small or large, rough or smooth, and tightly or loosely twisted. Loosely twisted yarns make a fabric that will wrinkle. L144: Tightly twisted ones do not wrinkle as easily. Yarn differences create changes in appearance, durability and texture. L145: The two most common methods of making fabric are by weaving or knitting. The way a fabric is constructed affects its durability, use, warmth or coolness, and appearance. L146: L147: Wovens L148: A woven fabric is made by interlacing two sets of yarns. This is where the lengthwise yarns and crosswise yarns cross each other at right angles. They go over and under, back and forth. L149: Lengthwise yarns form the foundation of the fabric and are usually stronger. They run parallel to the selvage, which is the finished edge. The selvage is made by doubling the number of lengthwise yarns. Crosswise yarns are perpendicular to the selvage. L150: L151: A plain weave is the most common method of making fabric. It is a basic one-under and one-over combination of a lengthwise and crosswise yarn. Examples are taffeta, broadcloth, and organdy. L152: L153: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 3 L154: Page 3 L155: L156: LESSON 3  CUTTING EDGE L157: The basket weave is a variation of the plain weave -- two or more yarns are carried together in a two under and two over weave. L158: L159: **Knits** L160: L161: Knitting is a method of fabric construction. Yarns are frequently texturized. This means that they have built-in crimps or coils that allow for some stretch in a fabric. Knit fabrics stretch. Some stretch in both directions, others will primarily stretch crosswise. Single knits are like hand knitting. They are sometimes called plain or jersey. L162: L163: **Texture** L164: Sight, hearing, smell and tough are all sensitive in some way to texture. Texture is the surface appeal of an object. Clothing texture can create several reactions. Your eyes respond to the look of the fabric. Your ears respond to the sound as the person moves. Your hands respond to how a fabric feels when you touch it. The way a fabric is constructed and the type of yarn used determines its texture. Every fabric has its own texture of feel, look, and sound. Frequently we refer to the "hand" of a fabric. L165: This refers to the weight, thickness, and how the fabric drapes. L166: Some comparison of fabrics could include terms such as coarse vs. fine, opaque vs. sheer, thin vs. bulky, soft vs. stiff, limp vs. crisp, cool vs. warm, shiny vs. dull, light vs. heavy, stretch vs. firm, spongy vs. firm, smooth vs. rough. L167: L168: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 3  Page 4 L169: L170: LESSON 3: CUTTING EDGE  Activity 1: Make a Checkerboard! L171: L172: L173: L174: L175: L176: L177: L178:
SUGGESTED AGE:5-8 years old
OBJECTIVES:Youth will be able to:
o describe how fabrics are made
o express individuality in selecting colors
o strengthen psychomotor skills
o demonstrate skills in following directions
o demonstrate left-right orientation skills
o improve group cooperation skills
MATERIALS:1 sheet of construction paper per child
2 colored sheets of bright 8½x11 paper per child
Scissors
Stapler
Various small scraps of fabric
Magnifying lens
MAKE A CHECKERBOARD Workbook page 12.
TIME:45 minutes
SETTING:Room with tables for children to complete work.
ADVANCE PREPARATION:Read Weaving Instructions for another easy method to use for a young child. Older children, may be able to cut paper and weave without attaching to a board. Test yourself first to know which method you want to use!
L179: INTRODUCTION L180: L181: The clothes we wear are made from different fabrics. Fabrics are made by several different ways. One way is by weaving yarns together. We are going to look at how fabrics are made and make a checkerboard to practice weaving. L182: L183: Do L184: L185: Make a CHECKERBOARD! L186: ♦ Give each child a piece of scrap fabric for them to examine under the magnifying glass. Tell them to look for the "weave" (show and explain this new term to them). L187: ♦ Give each child one piece of colored construction paper and two 8½ x 11 sheets of colored paper. L188: ♦ For one sheet, cut the colored 8½ x 11 sheets into eight strips almost to the top of the sheet. L189: ♦ Staple this sheet to the construction paper. L190: ♦ Cut the other sheet into 8 strips to use to weave. L191: L192: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 3  Page 5 L193: LESSON 3: CUTTING EDGE    Activity 1: Make a Checkerboard! L194: L195: ♦ Tell the child to weave the strips in and out of the stapled sheet like the fabric. L196:  Each strip should be stapled or glued at the end to hold it in place. L197:  The finished product should resemble a checker board. L198: ♦ Cut paper scraps into small squares to be used as checkers. L199: L200: REFLECT L201: L202: ♦ What is one way that fabrics are made? L203:  weaving L204: L205: ♦ Was it easy to weave the paper back and forth? Why or why not? L206: L207: APPLY L208: ♦ Would it take you a long time to weave threads together to make a piece of fabric? L209: L210: ♦ Think about all the clothes we wear and the fabric used. How are fabrics woven today? L211: L212: ♦ Look at other fabrics using a magnifying glass to see how they are made. L213: L214: ♦ Play checkers on the woven checker board. L215: L216: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 3  Page 6 L217: L218: LESSON 4 CHOICES L219: L220: Do L221: The following is suggested for using the activities in Lesson 4. Materials needed for each are listed within the activity. L222: ♦ Demonstrate a positive attitude about clothes with MY FAVORITE OUTFIT! L223: ♦ Identify appropriate uses of garments with SEASONAL COLLAGE, SUITCASE RELAY, ALL MIXED UP, and PASS-IT-AROUND SONG! L224: ♦ Identify the effects of color in COLOR MATCH, TALKING COLORS, COOL CARL, AND WARM WANDA! L225: ♦ Identify vertical, horizontal, diagonal, and curved lines in WHAT’S MY LINE! L226: ♦ Identify solids, stripes, plaids, and prints in MATCH ME! L227: L228: Reflect L229: After completing the activities in this lesson, help youth reflect on what they have learned with these questions: L230: L231: ♦ What are some reasons we like certain clothes? L232: color, fit L233: L234: ♦ Why is it important to where clothing that is appropriate to the season or activity? L235: comfort, safety, health L236: L237: ♦ Why would we want to wear colors that compliment each other? L238: to look good, fashion L239: L240: ♦ What are the four types of lines? L241: vertical, horizontal, diagonal, curved L242: ♦ What are cool and warm colors? L243: blue and green; red, yellow and orange L244: L245: ♦ What are the four general types of patterns of fabric? L246: solids, stripes, plaids, prints L247: L248: ♦ What are some ways that certain colors make you feel? L249: L250: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 4 Page 2 L251: L252: LESSON 5  CONSUMERISM L253: L254: BACKGROUND BASICS…Consumerism L255: **Labels** L256: A label is written information that is attached to an item, such as a garment. It provides information you need and want to know about the clothing you buy. By law most apparel items (some exceptions are hosiery, gloves, hats, and reversible garments) must have a label or labels with the following: L257: L258: - fiber content L259: - care L260: - country of origin L261: - registered identification number L262: Care, registered identification number, and country of origin must be permanently attached to the garment. Fiber content may be permanently attached or on a hangtag. L263: As you shop for clothing, labeling should be used to help you in making a decision of whether to purchase. The care instructions tell you how to properly clean the garment. Fiber content labels not only tell you what generic fibers have been used, but also in what percentage. Country of origin tells you the origin of the fabrics and where the apparel was made. The registered identification number is a number registered with the Federal Trade Commission, which tells you the name of the manufacturer. L264: Clothing labels are most frequently found at the neckline or waistline. However, in some instances they will be found on another seam. L265: **Fibers** L266: Fibers are where our fabrics and apparel begin. The generic name is the key word you need to know and understand when buying a textile product. It is the family name of the natural and manufactured fibers. The two most common cellulosic (plant) natural fibers are cotton and linen. The two most common protein (animal) natural fibers are wool and silk. The most common manufactured (cellulosic) is rayon. The most common manufactured (chemical) are polyester, nylon, and acrylic. These are the generic names. L267: Fibers may also have a trademark name that could be included on the label. A trademark (tradename) is a word or symbol copyrighted by the producer of the fiber. It serves to identify these products and to distinguish the textile product of one manufacturer from another. Trademarked fibers are protected by a quality control program. Examples are Acrilan® acrylic and Trevira® polyester. L268: L269: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 5  Page 3 L270: L271: LESSON 6  CARE L272: L273: BACKGROUND BASICS...Care L274: Did you know that proper care of clothing makes it last longer. Caring for your clothing involves: L275: L276: • proper care when you undress -- fold or hang or if soiled then place in the laundry basket L277: • learning the steps in doing the washing of clothes L278: • learning how to sort clothes L279: • learning about hanging clothes outside to dry L280: • learning to identify clothing that has stains L281: When you undress and the clothing is unsoiled, then you can hang it back in the closet or you can fold and place on a shelf or in a drawer. If you just toss it on the floor, the clothing will need to be ironed to remove the wrinkles. L282: L283: Washing Clothes... L284: L285: The steps in washing your clothing are: L286: • carefully read labels found on the clothing to determine how to wash, water temperature, products to use and/or how to dry L287: • sort clothing into "like" piles L288: • check clothing carefully for "things" in pockets or a stain L289: • zip zippers, button buttons L290: • decide on water temperature L291: • decide on wash cycle L292: • read laundry product labels and use recommended amount L293: • fill washing machine, add laundry products L294: • add clothing to be washed, do not overload L295: • remove clothing promptly to prevent wrinkling L296: Careful sorting of clothes is essential for a clean, lint-free wash, and for saving energy and money. If problems occur because they were not carefully sorted, you will have to do it again. Sometimes you can’t "undo" the problem. Take time to sort your laundry according to: L297: • color (whites with whites, lights with lights, darks with darks, brights with brights) L298: • soil (lightly soiled with lightly soiled, heavily soiled with heavily soiled) L299: • fabric type (delicates with delicates, heavy with heavy) L300: • tendency to lint (lint receivers from lint givers) L301: L302: Most clothing can be line dried. Line drying on a bright, clear day will give your clothing a fresh, clean smell. But some whites should not be line dried because of the optical L303: L304: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 6  Page 4 L305: LESSON 6  CARE L306: L307: brighteners used when manufacturing the fabric. Line drying saves wear and tear on clothing. Especially think about line drying garments you don’t want to shrink, clothing with elastic, and older clothing. If line drying, remember to smooth and pull clothes into shape. Bright colors should be turned wrong side out and hung in the shade to prevent bleaching of the color. L308: To fold clothes lay on a flat surface, smooth and pull gently into shape. Make as few folds as possible, so the garment will fit the storage space. Rolling knits is another option. L309: L310: **Stains...** L311: A stain is a spot on your clothing. It could be from spilling juice or other drink, mustard or other food item, oil or grease, candy or gum, dirt or grass. It is important to identify a stain on your clothing so the person doing the laundry will know to pre-treat before putting into the washing machine. Also, new stains are easier to remove. Sometimes an old stain cannot be removed. So it is better to remove stains soon. L312: If you have a stain on your clothing tell your mom right away. Remember that stains need to be treated immediately. Old stains sometimes cannot be removed. For washable garments blot off any excess stain and flush with tap water. L313: L314: **FOR WASHABLE GARMENTS --** Always read the garments care label and how to use products used in removing stains. Test on an inconspicuous seam to test colorfastness of the garment and the reaction to the products you will be using. L315: Grass -- Sponge then flush with drycleaning solvent. Rinse. Rub with detergent and launder with detergent and recommended bleach. L316: L317: Ketchup -- Gently scrape off excess. Sponge or soak in cool water. Rub with detergent and launder with detergent and appropriate bleach in hottest water recommended for fabric. L318: L319: Mustard -- Gently scrape off excess. Sponge or soak in cool water. Rub with detergent and launder with detergent and appropriate bleach in hottest water recommended for fabric. L320: Grape Juice -- Flush then soak in cool water. Rub with detergent and launder with detergent and appropriate bleach in the hottest water recommended for the fabric. Air dry, until you know stain has been removed. L321: L322: Ice Cream -- Sponge/flush with drycleaning solvent. Air dry. Rinse in cool water. Rub with laundry bar soap and launder with detergent and appropriate bleach in the hottest water recommended for fabric. L323: L324: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 6  Page 5 L325: LESSON 6 CARE L326: L327: Paint, Oil Base -- Gently scrape excess. Immediately sponge, then flush with paint solvent. Repeat, if needed. Air dry. Sponge with water. Rub with detergent and launder as usual. L328: L329: Mud -- Let dry, scrape/brush gently. Sponge with cool water. Rub with detergent. Launder with detergent and bleach, if not contrary to care label. L330: L331: Mending Basics... L332: Steps for Teaching Sew-Through Buttons: L333: • Use a double thread or single thread of either all purpose, topstitching, or buttonhole thread. L334: • Hide knot or secure thread under button. L335: • Bring thread up through hole allowing for shank (use toothpick or pin). L336: • Go through second hole taking thread through fabric. L337: • Continue stitching in the same place for 6 stitches. L338: • If you used a toothpick or pin remove, wind thread around stitches under button. L339: • Secure thread. L340: L341: SUGGESTED LITERATURE: L342: The following books are recommended for reading in conjunction with the various activities for Care. They should be available at your local public library. L343: L344: Berry, Joy Wilt. What to Do When Your Mom or Dad says--"Take Care of Your Clothes. Chicago: Children’s Press, 1982. L345: Children learn how to take proper care of their clothing so they will last longer, and so that their parents won’t get upset. L346: Brown, Craig McFarland. The Patchwork Farmer. New York: Greenwillow Books, 1989. L347: After ripping his overalls again and again in the course of his daily work, a farmer ends up with a colorful patchwork pair. L348: L349: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 6 Page 6 L350: L351: LESSON 6: CLOTHING CARE  Activity 2: Clothing Pin-Ups L352: L353: L354: L355: L356: L357: L358: L359:
SUGGESTED AGE:5-8 years old
OBJECTIVES:Youth will be able to:
o identify clothing parts
o develop classification skills
MATERIALS:Felt board with pin-ups of clothing garments & parts (sleeve cuffs, buttons, collars, pant cuffs, shirt pockets, zippers, and jean pockets)
Hook and loop fasteners
Blindfold
TIME:30 minutes
SETTING:A large area cleared of tables and chairs
ADVANCED PREPARATION:Cut out felt shapes of clothing parts and enlarged felt body shape. Attach hook and loop fastener to clothing parts. Attach clothing Pin-up Garments to felt board.
L360: INTRODUCTION L361: L362: Knowing the parts of clothing is necessary for proper care. By playing Clothing Pin-Ups, we will identify the different parts of the clothing in a fun and exciting way. L363: L364: Do L365: L366: Play "CLOTHING PIN-UPS!" L367: ♦ Give a child one of the clothing parts cut-outs to identify. Blindfold that child and spin them around three times. L368: ♦ The other children should stand back so not to be in the way of the blindfolded child. L369: ♦ After spinning the child around, point him/her in the direction of the felt board with the Clothing Pin-Up Garments attached and tell them to go. L370: ♦ The child should then attempt to find the felt board and put the clothing part on the garment in the right place. L371: ♦ After the child has pinned the clothing part on the board, the blindfold should be removed for them to see how close they were to the actual location. L372: ♦ The child should then move the part to the place where it belongs. L373: ♦ After the group is satisfied that the clothing part is in the proper place, the part should be removed. L374: ♦ Give a different part of clothing to another child and start over again. L375: ♦ This should be continued until every child has had at least one opportunity to play the game. L376: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 6  Page 9 L377: L378: LESSON 6: CLOTHING CARE  Activity 2: Clothing Pin-Ups L379: L380: REFLECT L381: L382: ♦ Why is it important to know the parts of our clothes? L383:  To follow directions when caring for them L384: L385: ♦ What are the clothing parts we named today? L386:  Sleeve cuffs, pant cuffs, shirt pockets, jeans pockets, zippers, collars, buttons L387: L388: APPLY L389: L390: ♦ Name some other clothing parts it is necessary to know. L391: L392: ♦ Share what you learned with a friend. L393: L394: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES, Lesson 6  Page 10 L395: L396: 4-H FUN WITH CLOTHES L397: # Clothing Pin - Ups ! # Компактная форма SOURCE-пакета

Это точная форма уже действующих six/four/source/peer требований, а не новая процедура приёмки. Для знакомства со схемой не печатать целиком старые candidate/sourceproof/peer-snapshot. Смысловые основания автор пишет сам; поля и hashes формирует инструментом. Никаких автоматически выставленных PASS.

Три файла: `candidate.json`, `sourceproof.json`, `peer-snapshot.json`. В каждом — один и тот же фактический `sourceNativeId`, `topicId`, `cycle`, ID карточки. Native ID подтверждается coordinator по реальному session_meta, а не копируется из task owner. До START никаких записей.

## Хэши: три разных представления

```python
def canonical_sha(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False,
        sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
def file_sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
def body_sha(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
```

- Карточка, literal (включая строку), triple и rows: `canonical_sha`.
- Файл: `file_sha`. Не путать с хэшем содержимого строки внутри JSON.
- Полный original tool body, извлечённый по JSON Pointer: `body_sha`. JSON-кавычки и escaping в этот hash не входят.
- Никогда не переписывать hex вручную и не копировать hash между разными представлениями.

## Candidate

`entries[0]` содержит `id`, `topicId`, `sourceOrder`, `status`, `beforeCard`, `beforeHash`, `proposedCard`, `afterHash`, `fieldGroups`.

`status` — `READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW` либо точный `HOLD`; quality credit всегда0. Before — действительный preimage текущего назначения. Frozen ID/topic/order/difficulty/numeric key проверить по selection. Labels не заморожены глобально; править хороший текст без конкретного дефекта нельзя.

Использовать только dict-форму `fieldGroups`: ровно шесть ключей, каждый с вычисленными `beforeCanonicalSHA256` / `afterCanonicalSHA256`:

```python
def groups(card):
    return {
      'prompt_ordered_answers_key': {
        'prompt': card['prompt'],
        'answers': [a['text'] for a in card['answers']],
        'correctIndex': card['correctIndex']},
      'explanation': card['explanation'],
      **{'note'+str(k): a['note'] for k,a in enumerate(card['answers'])}}
```

## Sourceproof

`rawSources[]`: `path`, `url`, `sha256` (реальный file SHA), `captureReadProvenance`, `locator`. Для JSON-container также `completeOutputPointer` и `completeOutputSHA256` (= body SHA). Для общего capture перечислить все реальные URL/locators; не терять их из-за одинакового file path.

`path` — только существующий устойчивый файл. Не `journal item N`, не `file#pointer`, не URL. JSON Pointer хранится отдельным полем. Новый raw сохранять один раз отдельным файлом до создания packet; не делать self-hash текущего sourceproof. Сохранённые immutable full contexts переиспользовать по file/pointer, не копировать в каждый packet.

`entries[0].literalGroups[]`: ровно шесть объектов `group`, `literal`, `literalSHA256`, `primaryGround`, `sourcePaths`, `locator`. Literal — фактическое значение из `groups(proposedCard)`. PrimaryGround объясняет конкретный вывод, границы и qualifiers из полного первичного контекста, а не наличие ссылки.

`fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments[]`: слоты0..3, каждый содержит `fullPrompt`, `answer`, `note`, `tripleSHA256`, `grammar`, `plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefulness`, `sourcePaths`, `locator`.

Triple = `{'prompt': fullPrompt, 'answer': answer, 'note': note}`. SourcePaths — голые file paths из rawSources; конкретный JSON Pointer/строки остаются в locator. В оценке явно обосновать грамматику, правдоподобие и единственность ключа, истинность и полезность справки именно для этого варианта. Истинный соседний тематический факт сам по себе недостаточен.

Отдельно `correctNoteNewFact` и `absoluteDifficulty` с конкретным собственным основанием. Факт правильной справки — сверх всего prompt/key; совпадение с explanation само по себе не запрет. Source presence/посещаемость/относительное сравнение не доказывают EASY.

Указанные file hashes должны соответствовать записанной текущей версии на момент передачи.
- Все100 текущих карточек темы сохранять инструментом, не печатать их целиком только ради формата. `actualCurrentPeers` — полные актуальные body/hash/id/topicId для peer bindings.

- Новое изменение в другом потоке требует только машинного refresh inventory и проверки действительно затронутых смысловых связей. Это точная форма уже действующих six/four/source/peer требований, а не новая процедура приёмки. Для знакомства со схемой не печатать целиком старые candidate/sourceproof/peer-snapshot. Три файла: `candidate.json`, `sourceproof.json`, `peer-snapshot.json`. В каждом — один и тот же фактический `sourceNativeId`, `topicId`, `cycle`, ID карточки. Native ID подтверждается coordinator по реальному session_meta, а не копируется из task owner. До START никаких записей.

## Хэши: три разных представления

```python
def canonical_sha(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False,
        sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
def file_sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
def body_sha(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
```

- Карточка, literal (включая строку), triple и rows: `canonical_sha`.
- Файл: `file_sha`. Не путать с хэшем содержимого строки внутри JSON.
- Полный original tool body, извлечённый по JSON Pointer: `body_sha`. JSON-кавычки и escaping в этот hash не входят.
- Никогда не переписывать hex вручную и не копировать hash между разными представлениями.

## Candidate

`entries[0]` содержит `id`, `topicId`, `sourceOrder`, `status`, `beforeCard`, `beforeHash`, `proposedCard`, `afterHash`, `fieldGroups`.
